name: Deepwater Smuggler's Transit Full Kit
description: A battered lake-freight worker's layered kit — oilskin outer shell in faded slate-green over a scanner-dampening liner, worn canvas cargo trousers with six false-bottom pockets, and steel-toed deck boots with hollowed heels. The jacket's lining is woven with signal-scatter mesh that reads as standard industrial polyweave on checkpoint scanners. Nothing about it says criminal; everything about it says someone who moves cargo for a living.
functionality: Six false-bottom cargo pockets, scanner-dampening liner, and hollow heel compartments hold contraband rated up to 2kg without triggering standard checkpoint sensors.
what_it_says: This person loads and unloads freight for twelve hours a day and has nothing worth inspecting.
story_hooks: A checkpoint officer keeps waving the wearer through — until one shift, he doesn't.
The hollow heels contain a data chip that wasn't supposed to be there when the courier picked up the shipment.

physical_description.visual_profile: A weathered, utilitarian ensemble that reads as working-class dockside labor—deliberately unremarkable and built for concealment. The silhouette is broad-shouldered and functional, with strategic layering that suggests someone accustomed to water exposure and long shifts. Everything about it broadcasts 'cargo handler' rather than 'smuggler,' which is precisely the point.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and utilitarian throughout—the oilskin jacket drapes with room for movement and hidden bulk, cargo trousers sit comfortably at the waist with excess fabric in the legs, boots are sturdy and break-in worn. Designed for function over form, with no tailoring that would suggest corpo wealth.
physical_description.primary_material: Faded oilskin outer shell (lake-resistant, wax-treated canvas blend) over scanner-dampening synthetic liner; heavy-duty canvas cargo trousers; scuffed steel-toed deck boots with genuine rubber soles.
physical_description.texture: The oilskin has a weathered, slightly tacky surface with visible creasing and minor cracks from age; canvas shows soft fraying at seams and a broken-in suppleness; boot leather is cracked and salt-stained, with rubber soles worn uneven from thousands of dock hours.
physical_description.color_scheme: Faded slate-green oilskin with darker staining and salt-spray bleaching; tan-gray canvas trousers with rust-colored cargo pocket trim; charcoal steel-toed boots. Everything is muted and naturally aged—no bright accents or chrome.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty brass and steel hardware throughout: oilskin jacket fastens with a combination of friction-fit toggles and corroded brass snaps; cargo trousers have a worn brass belt loop system and button fly; boots lace with weathered cord, partially frayed.
distinctive_features: Signal-scatter mesh woven into jacket lining—registers as standard polyweave on port authority scanners
Six false-bottom cargo pockets in trousers with hidden mag-seal compartments beneath standard pocket openings
Hollowed steel-toed heels in boots (capacity: ~200 grams of compact contraband or data storage)
Jacket interior lined with scanner-dampening synthetic—blocks passive RFID/tracking signals
Oil stains, salt residue, and minor tears that look like honest wear, not intentional camouflage
Reinforced stress points at seams and pocket corners—designed to take abuse without splitting
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 (working class to sub-grade). The outfit costs under 150Φ on the street market and screams 'legitimate dock labor.' No logos, no chrome, no augmentation tech visible—this is peak low-profile.
physical_description.cultural_context: Dockside labor, independent freight handlers, and by extension, those who move things 'unofficially' through the Great Lakes supply chain. Wearing this in a corpo office would be instantly suspicious; wearing it at a cargo terminal makes you invisible. The GLMZ's mixed-heritage dockworker communities have worn variations of this kit for decades—it's authentic enough to pass even casual scrutiny.
physical_description.condition_typical: Always worn, never pristine. The gear is actively weathered—salt-stained, oil-spotted, with minor rips and fraying that are routine maintenance, not signs of poverty. A fresh, clean version would look suspicious. This outfit should look like it's been through fifty supply runs.
